abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of ten statements. Let K be a number field of degree 9 containing a totally real cubic field L and a cubic field M with one real place. Then K = LM has signature (3, 3), and its nine embeddings are the pairs (lambda, mu). A slot assignment, fixed by a labelling of L's embeddings and a non-real embedding mu_1 of M, places the nine conjugates of x in K in a 3 x 3 Hermitian array, the symbol of x; the symbol of x^-1 is its entrywise (Hadamard) inverse. (1) For every finite index type, a positive semidefinite complex matrix with no zero entry has positive semidefinite Hadamard inverse iff it is w w* (rank one); (2) for every complex matrix with no zero entry (positive semidefiniteness not assumed), the Schur multipliers of the matrix and of its Hadamard inverse are both completely positive iff it is w w*. Statements 1-2 are supporting lemmas. (3) The setting: L and M are linearly disjoint, L M = K, and K has 3 real and 3 complex places. (4) The slot assignment exists, is a bijection Fin 3 x Fin 3 ~ (K -> C) with real diagonal and conjugate-symmetric slots, and is unique. (5) For x != 0 in K, the symbol of x is rank one iff N_{K/L}(x) and N_{K/M}(x) are one and the same positive rational number. (6) For a unit u, the symbol is rank one iff N_{K/L}(u) = N_{K/M}(u) = 1. (7) These units H are torsion-free and their logarithmic embedding spans a Z-module of rank 2, so H is isomorphic to Z^2 (the isomorphism is not itself a Lean term). (8) For a unit u, the Schur multipliers of the symbols of u and of u^-1 are both completely positive iff u is in H. (9) There is a unit of infinite order all of whose powers run both ways. (10) The degree-four contrast: in a field with two real places and one complex place, both Schur multipliers of the 2 x 2 place symbol of a unit u and of u^-1 are completely positive iff u is positive at both real places and |sigma(u)| = 1. Statements 4-6, 8 and 9 hold for every labelling and every non-real mu_1. The compositum place bookkeeping is ported, with citation, from the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012; it is not re-proved. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by a unit; if a unit acts by multiplication on a Hermitian register of its places and an admissible tick must be completely positive, then in degree four a tick u != 1 runs both ways only through a conjugate on the unit circle (Salem type); in a field such as Q(Q), Q^4 = Q + 1, the only such elements are +-1 (not proved in this entry; it follows from statement 17 of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, since Q(Q) is contained in Q(rho, Q)), so there the arithmetic gives time a direction; in degree nine a rank-two group of units runs both ways, so the direction is not a property of arithmetic in general: it rests on the degree-four shape and on Q(Q) having no conjugate on the unit circle. The ticks are completely positive, not trace-non-increasing. Companion of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), whose README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.

Its compared statements include the chirality of the Padovan substitution (the arrow at the level of the settled word); this entry gives it at the level of the tick in Q(Q), as complete positivity in one direction only, and shows it is not forced by arithmetic in general: in the degree-nine shape a rank-two group of units runs both ways. The README's Scope section is that entry's, verbatim; its one relative link, to the paper directory, now points into the companion repository at the registered revision. Mathlib at the pin has no Schur-multiplier complete-positivity criterion, no Salem predicate and no relative-norm product formula for a compositum; the entry proves the latter from Algebra.norm_eq_prod_embeddings.

title: The Arithmetic of Time: reversible units of a degree-nine field. The units of K = LM (L, M cubic) with rank-one Hermitian symbol are exactly those of trivial relative norm to L and to M, a group of rank two, and exactly those whose Schur multipliers run both ways
